Both code blocks match lines 6-23 and 29-38 character-for-character.

StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest ... }`. Registered first in the pipeline: Program.cs `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>();`.

OrderServiceTests.cs:37-43 `PlaceOrderAsync_NoItems_Throws`: `var service = new OrderService(new FakeOrderRepository(), new FakeNotifier()); await Assert.ThrowsAsync<ArgumentException>(() => service.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId: 1, items: []));`. Usings are only DonHang.Domain and Xunit; DonHang.Tests.csproj references only DonHang.Domain, so no ASP.NET Core type is involved.

OrderService.cs has exactly two public methods, PlaceOrderAsync and CancelOrderAsync; its only types are Order, OrderItem, IOrderRepository, INotifier, ArgumentException, KeyNotFoundException, DateTimeOffset. DonHang.Domain.csproj is `Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk"` with no PackageReference/ProjectReference, so no ASP.NET Core or EF Core type is reachable.

OrdersController.cs:21 `int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!)`; :58-63 `private static OrderDto ToDto(Order order) => new(...)`. OrderService.cs:10 empty-items throw, :16 `Status = "new"`, :21 `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed")`. Try-it expected answer (1,4 controller; 2,3,5 service) matches.

Design principle, restating the glossary definition of service-layer ("taking and returning plain data with no HTTP involved") that the lesson defines in section 3; not a versioned behaviour. Consistent with the repo: PlaceOrderAsync/CancelOrderAsync take int/List<OrderItem>, return Order, and throw BCL exceptions.

Follows from the premise: if the parameter were an HTTP request type, every call site must supply one. "token included" in section 6 holds because the customer id currently comes from the token's `sub` (OrdersController.cs:21), so a request-taking service would read it from there.

issues.text: Key is correct (c) and option d is still wrong, but the new explanation for d is literally false: DonHang.Domain.csproj uses Microsoft.NET.Sdk with ImplicitUsings enabled, whose default namespaces include System.Net.Http (refs dotnet-docs core/project-sdk/overview.md:148), so HTTP types such as HttpRequestMessage are available. What the project lacks is ASP.NET Core's request types. The lesson itself only says the service 'does not know that HTTP exists', which is fine.
issues.quote: C# allows it; the Domain project simply has no HTTP types available, by design.
issues.fix: en d: "C# allows it; `OrderService` simply uses no HTTP types, by design." vi d: "C# cho phép; chỉ là `OrderService` cố ý không dùng kiểu HTTP nào."

issues.fix: Add one sentence after the section 5 code block: the tests pass their own small classes that implement IOrderRepository and INotifier (the interfaces from the DIP lesson), so no database or real notification is needed.
